answer: Model attestations as a weighted graph and propagate trust with a random walk stopped after at most \(k\) steps; a vertex’s influence is then limited by reachable trusted mass, not its raw identity count. A sybil cluster joined to honest vertices by a sparse cut has low conductance, so few walk paths enter it; conductance-based mixing and min-cut transitivity bounds limit its aggregate voting weight. A prism diagram can expose the bottleneck, while “sonnet” names the bounded-walk rule.
